blocks.content: The Government of India Act of 1935 served as a major source for the structural part of the Constitution of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Regulating Act of 1773 designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General of Bengal' and established a Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774.
The Charter Act of 1833 created the office of the Governor-General of India, ending the commercial activities of the East India Company.
The Government of India Act of 1858 ended the Company Rule, abolished the Board of Control and Court of Directors, and created the office of the Secretary of State for India.
The Indian Councils Act of 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms) introduced a system of communal representation for Muslims via separate electorates.
The Government of India Act of 1935 provided for the establishment of an All-India Federation and divided powers into Federal, Provincial, and Concurrent Lists.

rows: Abolished in Provinces; proposed at the Center
Introduced Bicameralism in 6 out of 11 Provinces
Limited to property, tax, or education criteria
Extended to approximately 10% of total population

items: Dyarchy was introduced in the provinces by the Government of India Act of 1919 and replaced by Provincial Autonomy under the Government of India Act of 1935.
Lord William Bentinck was the first Governor-General of India (Charter Act 1833), whereas Lord Canning became the first Viceroy of India (GOI Act 1858).
Communal electorates were introduced in 1909 for Muslims, extended in 1919 to Sikhs, Indian Christians, and Anglo-Indians, and further extended in 1935 to depressed classes and women.
